rounds.text: Tech Mahindra is experiencing a powerful acceleration in foundational profitability, highlighted by compounded profit growth reaching 27% over the trailing twelve months and operating margins expanding to 17% against 9% three years earlier [E21, E30]. This earnings momentum is fully backed by cash generation, as demonstrated by a cash conversion ratio of 1.28x alongside Rs 5,626 Cr in free cash flow for March 2026 [E34, E36]. The balance sheet remains exceptionally robust with borrowings at just Rs 2,184 Cr, supporting a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.07x and a healthy 2.82% dividend yield [E4, E37, E39]. Operational execution is further validated by a stellar rules-based screen score of 91 out of 100 and a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E51, E63]. Management reinforces this confidence by reiterating an FY27 EBIT margin target of 15% and reporting a 34.8% year-on-year surge in last-12-month deal wins to reach US$4,270 million [E75, E88]. Conceded: the company has delivered a poor sales growth of 8.46% over the past five years and a low return on equity of 13.3% over the last 3 years [E61, E62].

Tech Mahindra is priced for perfection on a chart that is stretched to its limits, sitting 95% of the way up its 52-week range [E48] at a rich P/E of 31x [E1] that towers well above the sector benchmark of 20.61x [E6]. This lofty valuation relies on an aggressive forward expectation, with a reverse DCF revealing that today's share price already bakes in a 14.6% earnings growth rate, vastly outstripping the modest 2.0% assumed in the base case [E47]. Beneath the surface of these high multiples, long-term operational momentum has stalled out, highlighted by a sluggish 3-year compounded sales growth of just 2% [E16] and a meager 1% compounded profit growth over the same 3-year window [E20]. Furthermore, institutional conviction is quietly eroding, evidenced by foreign institutional holding dropping from 24.58% in Dec 2023 to 20.76% as of Sep 2026 [E42]. Conceded: the company boasts a robust ROA of 11.42% beating the sector benchmark of 6.07% [E8], and foreign outflows are partially offset by domestic institutional holdings increasing to 35.68% [E43].

Conceded: the share price sits near its 52-week high [E48] and trades at a P/E of 31x [E1]. However, that premium valuation is entirely justified by superior return metrics, with an ROE of 18.62% crushing the sector benchmark of 10.38% [E9] and an ROA of 11.42% outperforming the sector's 6.07% [E8]. While the bear points to sluggish 3-year historical metrics [E16, E20], it ignores a dramatic inflection point in current execution: trailing twelve-month sales growth has surged to 14% [E17] and profit growth has exploded to 27% [E21]. Furthermore, operating margins are structurally expanding, rising by 8 percentage points over three years to 17% in the TTM period [E30], driven by efficiency programs and strong volume growth [E86]. Conceded: foreign institutional holdings declined over the period [E42], but this outflow has been aggressively absorbed by domestic institutions whose holdings rose to 35.68% [E43], creating positive overall institutional money flow [E44]. Finally, the business is exceptionally well-capitalized with a minimal debt-to-equity ratio of 0.07x [E37] and generated robust free cash flow of Rs 5,626 Cr [E36], backed by surging last-12-month deal wins of $4,270 million up 34.8% year-on-year [E88].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth has reached 27% [E21] and ROE outperforms the sector at 18.62% [E9]. However, the bull's reliance on these short-term metrics masks a severe multi-year growth deficit, where compounded sales growth over 3 years limps at 2% [E16] and profit growth over 5 years is a stagnant 2% [E19]. Conceded: deal wins stand at $4,270 million [E88], yet this momentum has failed to translate into historical top-line expansion, which flags a poor sales growth of just 8.46% over the past five years [E61]. Furthermore, the bull dismisses institutional outflows, but foreign institutions have dumped their stake from 24.58% to 20.76% [E42], reflecting waning confidence among global smart money. The bull's enthusiasm for the 31x P/E multiple [E1] ignores the severe valuation disconnect flagged by the DCF model, which puts intrinsic value at Rs 726 against a market price of Rs 1,811, resulting in an alarming margin of safety of -149.6% [E45, E46]. Finally, the reverse DCF exposes the precarious nature of this pricing, showing that today's market price already demands an aggressive 14.6% earnings growth rate—far eclipsing the 2.0% assumed in the base case [E47].

Conceded: compounded sales growth over 3 years is 2% [E16] and profit growth over 5 years is 2% [E19]. However, focusing solely on past multi-year lulls ignores the explosive acceleration happening right now, evidenced by trailing twelve-month profit growth surging to 27% [E21] and quarterly net profit jumping 34% year-on-year [E66]. Conceded: foreign institutional holdings moved from 24.58% to 20.76% [E42], but this outflow has been heavily absorbed and counterbalanced by domestic institutions expanding their stake from 28.91% to 35.68% [E43], driving overall institutional money flow into positive territory [E44]. Conceded: a standard discounted cash flow model yields an intrinsic value of Rs 726 [E45], but this mechanical calculation completely discounts the company's surging operational momentum, including a 34.8% year-on-year expansion in last-12-month deal wins to $4,270 million [E88] and a robust operating cash flow of Rs 6,172 Cr fully backing profits at 1.28x conversion [E34, E35]. Furthermore, the bear's reliance on reverse DCF assumptions ignores tangible margin expansion, with operating margins climbing to 18% in TTM from 9% three years prior [+8 pp] [E30] and management firmly tracking toward its 15% full-year EBIT margin target [E75].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth surged to 27% [E21] and net profit jumped 34% year-on-year [E66]. However, this cyclical rebound masks a multi-year structural stagnation featuring a 3-year compounded sales growth of just 2% [E16], 5-year compounded profit growth of 2% [E19], and a 5-year sales growth flagged as poor at 8.46% [E61]. Conceded: domestic institutions increased their stake to 35.68% [E43], but this occurred alongside a severe exodus of foreign institutions slashing their holdings from 24.58% to 20.76% [E42]. Conceded: last-12-month deal wins reached $4,270 million [E88] and cash conversion stands at 1.28x [E34], but these operational metrics do not validate a price trading at a rich P/E of 31x [E1], a P/B of 5.98x [E2], and a steep -149.6% margin of safety under DCF valuation [E45, E46]. Finally, while operating margins expanded to 18% [E30], the reverse DCF indicates that today's price already aggressively prices in 14.6% earnings growth against a realistic 2.0% base case, exposing investors to severe multiple contraction risk if growth normalizes [E47].
